title: Privilege Sweep Automation — Retrospective and Next Steps
content:
Purpose and scope:
This doc is a working retrospective on the first automated privileged access sweep we ran as part of Q1 least-privilege recertification. It summarizes what we did, what worked, what failed, gaps in the current RBAC v2 implementation and audit pipeline, and concrete next steps to reach a stable quarterly automation cadence.

Background (short):
- Goal: reduce manual effort for quarterly privileged access recertification by automating evidence collection, reviewer assignment, and SIEM-forwarding of audit artifacts.
- Scope for this run: users with admin-capable roles across Console, Dedicated control plane, and Private deployment control plane (approx 140 identities).
- Tools used: internal recertification service (alpha), RBAC v2 role-mapper, audit-log-export microservice, Splunk for SIEM ingestion, Jira for tasking.

What we automated in this sweep:
1) Role graph extraction from RBAC v2 (daily snapshot).
2) Mapping of role capabilities to privilege categories (admin, infra, data-access, support).
3) Evidence bundle assembly: last 90 days of action logs per principal, active sessions, MFA status, resource ownership tags.
4) Assignment of reviewers based on resource ownership and team mappings.
5) Export of a minimal recertification artifact to Splunk for retention and correlation with detection rules.

Successes:
- Role graph extraction pipeline is stable: the RBAC v2 API responses are deterministic and JSON schema is consistent with the role-mapper.
- Reviewer auto-assignment matched manual assignments for 82% of principals (saves ~6 hours of coordinator work).
- Evidence bundles contained sufficient action samples for most admin roles — reviewers could make decisions without requesting more logs in 68% of cases.
- SIEM export schema allowed us to correlate recert events with high-risk login events (worked well for two real incidents flagged during the run).

Failures and friction points:
- Audit log schema gaps: several event types emitted by the serving runtime (cache/kv-cache mutations, model-variant fallback events) lack a consistent actor field. Those events appeared in evidence bundles as "unknown_actor" and forced manual lookup.
- Time window mismatch: RBAC snapshot was taken at T0 but evidence logs pulled for T0–90d. For ~12 users role changes within the window caused mismatches (e.g., reviewers saw activity under an old role).
- SIEM field mapping drift: Splunk sourcetypes configured for "recert_artifact_v1" expected an "actor_email" string; our export used "principal_id" for some identities (service accounts). This broke some dashboards and retention rules.
- UX: reviewers found the evidence bundle UI clunky — hard to quickly see whether an action was administrative vs informational.

Technical gaps (detail):
1) Audit logs need canonical actor normalization: map (user.email | user.id | service_account.name) -> actor.{id,email,type}. This should be enforced at the audit-export microservice and validated against the audit-log-schema.
2) RBAC v2 snapshot process needs atomicity: either freeze-policy or tag snapshot with "snapshot_version" and attach it to bundles so reviewers know which role graph the evidence was evaluated against.
3) SIEM export should publish a versioned schema (recert_export_v2) and maintain a compatibility shim for recert_export_v1. Update Splunk parsing rules and dashboards to accept both fields (actor_email OR principal_id).
4) Evidence sampling size: for low-activity principals we need to optionally increase window to 180 days or include resource-change events (role assignment events) so reviewers have context.

Process and governance notes:
- Reviewer SLAs: We attempted 14-day SLAs; 30% of reviews were late. Root cause: reviewer capacity mismatch and unclear escalation path. Proposal: auto-escalation to team lead at day 7 and coordinator reminder at day 3.
- Exception handling: currently exceptions are captured in a free-text Jira ticket. We should standardize exception reasons (e.g., long-term-contractor, emergency-access, pending-offboarding) and codify them into the recert service to allow trending.

SIEM/export and detection considerations:
- Example Splunk query to find recert artifacts with unknown actor:
  index=recert sourcetype=recert_export_v2 actor.email=\"\" OR actor.email=NULL OR actor.type=\"unknown\" | stats count by principal_id, role
- Recommend creating a scheduled detection that joins recert export events with authn failures and admin API usage to flag reviewers who re-certify high-risk principals within a short window.
- Retention: recert bundles must be retained for 13 months for audit. Confirm Splunk index lifecycle policy and ensure evidence keys are encrypted-at-rest with customer KMS mapping when exported for Private deployments.

Action items (owners & target dates):
- PRI-1: Add canonical actor normalization to audit-export microservice and add tests (owner: Daniel Kim) — target: 2025-03-20.
- PRI-2: Add snapshot_version tag to RBAC v2 extractor and include in evidence bundles (owner: Marcus Lee) — target: 2025-03-15.
- PRI-3: Publish recert_export_v2 schema and update Splunk parsing rules; create compatibility shim (owner: Sofia Alvarez + Observability) — target: 2025-03-28.
- PRI-4: Implement reviewer auto-escalation workflow in recert service and add standard exception taxonomy (owner: Security Ops) — target: 2025-04-05.
- PRI-5: UX follow-up: quick view summary in reviewer UI showing "top admin actions" and a heatmap of action types (owner: Product - security console) — target: 2025-04-15.

Open questions / decisions needed:
- Should service accounts be surfaced differently (separate reviewer pool) or continue to be mixed with human identities? (impact: reviewer expertise, SLA)
- Policy: what is the default exception expiry for temporary emergency access? Proposal: 30 days with mandatory re-eval.

Notes for RBAC v2 roadmap:
- Add role provenance metadata (created_by, created_at, parent_role) to help investigators determine how a high-privilege role was minted.
- Add a lightweight "permission intent" field on roles so reviewers see why a role exists (operational, migration-support, legacy).

Appendix (quick snippets):
- Confluence links: https://confluence.redwood.com/display/SEC/RBAC+v2+Design+Notes
- Jira tickets referenced: SEC-3421 (recert infra), SEC-3477 (audit-schema normalization), OBS-904 (splunk parsing update)
- Slack thread: #sec-recert Q1 sweep — thread ts 1716200000 (see linked_conversation in Confluence page)

Summary / proposed next milestone:
By completing the four engineering PRI- tasks above and the UX improvements, we should be able to run the next quarterly sweep entirely automated (evidence collection -> reviewer assignment -> decision recording -> SIEM export) with <10% manual interventions. Target this for the end of Q2 with a cross-functional dry run two weeks prior.

Notes to self: push the recert_export_v2 schema through the design review tomorrow, ask Observability to give a hard bounce window for Splunk changes, and prep a short TL;DR for the Security all-hands.
